title: Completion-isomorphism and raw-localization transport of a compatible adjunction square
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $t\in A$, and $B=A[1/t]$. Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be $A$-linear categories and $\mathcal C',\mathcal D'$ be $B$-linear categories, meaning that their Hom groups are modules over the indicated ring and composition is bilinear. A linear functor is one that is linear on every Hom module [def-weil-linear-functor]. Let $P:\mathcal C\rightleftarrows\mathcal D:Q$ be adjoint $A$-linear functors, with unit $\eta$ and counit $\epsilon$, and let $P':\mathcal C'\rightleftarrows\mathcal D':Q'$ be adjoint $B$-linear functors, with unit $\eta'$ and counit $\epsilon'$. Let $F_C:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C'$ and $F_D:\mathcal D\to\mathcal D'$ be $A$-linear functors, using $A\to B$ on the targets. Specify natural isomorphisms $\alpha:F_DP\cong P'F_C$ and $\beta:F_CQ\cong Q'F_D$ satisfying
$$Q'(\alpha_N)\beta_{PN}F_C(\eta_N)=\eta'_{F_CN},\qquad F_D(\epsilon_M)=\epsilon'_{F_DM}P'(\beta_M)\alpha_{QM}.$$
Let $\widetilde P:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be $A$-linear and $\gamma:P\xrightarrow{\sim}\widetilde P$ a specified natural isomorphism. Then $\widetilde P\dashv Q$ has the transported adjunction characterized by
$$\operatorname{adj}_{\widetilde P,Q}(f)=\operatorname{adj}_{P,Q}(f\gamma_N),\qquad \widetilde\eta_N=Q(\gamma_N)\eta_N,\qquad\widetilde\epsilon_M=\epsilon_M\gamma_{QM}^{-1}.$$
With $\widetilde\alpha_N=\alpha_NF_D(\gamma_N^{-1})$ the comparison square still satisfies both displayed adjunction equations, with $P,\alpha,\eta,\epsilon$ replaced by $\widetilde P,\widetilde\alpha,\widetilde\eta,\widetilde\epsilon$.
Use the raw scalar localizations [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization], whose objects are unchanged and whose Hom modules are tensored with $B$, with no idempotent completion. The transported functors extend to $\widetilde P_B\dashv Q_B$ with unit $\widetilde\eta_N\otimes1$ and counit $\widetilde\epsilon_M\otimes1$. The functors $F_C,F_D$ extend to $B$-linear functors $\overline F_C,\overline F_D$ by $\overline F_W(u/t^n)=t^{-n}F_W(u)$. There are natural comparison isomorphisms $\overline\alpha:\overline F_D\widetilde P_B\cong P'\overline F_C$ and $\overline\beta:\overline F_CQ_B\cong Q'\overline F_D$ whose components at each unchanged object are respectively $\widetilde\alpha_N$ and $\beta_M$. They satisfy both adjunction equations for the localized unit and counit and the unchanged primed adjunction. These assertions also apply to adjunctions restricted from ambient categories to stable full subcategories. Composition is right to left.

proof.text: Transport the given adjunction along gamma with Adjunction.ofNatIsoLeft. Its homEquiv formula is homEquiv_ofNatIsoLeft_apply, and its unit and counit formulas hold by definition. Define alpha-tilde as isoWhiskerRight gamma.symm FD composed with alpha. Naturality of beta at gamma.hom, inverse cancellation and the original unit equation give the transported unit equation. Functoriality and the original counit equation give the transported counit equation.

Extend each A-linear functor Ptilde and Q on tensor Hom modules by LinearMap.baseChange. The pure-tensor formula is b tensor f mapped to b tensor F(f). Identity preservation is immediate. For composition, induction on each tensor reduces to the pure-tensor composition formula of the raw scalar localization and F.map_comp. The Hom maps are localized-ring linear, hence additive.

For each semilinear functor FC or FD into a category already linear over B, use TensorProduct.liftAddHom directly on the pairing (b,f) mapped to b smul F.map f. Balancing is the given scalar equation together with commutativity in B and associativity of scalar multiplication. Tensor induction proves B-linearity and composition preservation; identities follow from 1 smul F.map(id)=id. This directly constructs FCbar and FDbar, without localizing the primed categories at 1.

For B-linear additive functors on a raw scalar localization, a family of components natural on 1 tensor f is natural on all morphisms. Indeed b tensor f equals b smul (1 tensor f), so linearity and bilinearity reduce its naturality square to the given square; tensor induction handles zero and sums. Apply this to the tensor-with-one unit and counit. Their triangles reduce by the pure-tensor composition formula to the original triangles, constructing the localized adjunction with exactly its prescribed components.

Apply the same naturality argument to the original components of alpha-tilde and beta, using B-linearity of the primed functors. NatIso.ofComponents supplies the two localized comparison isomorphisms. Each component and each object map is definitionally the specified one. Finally FCbar(1 tensor unit)=FC(unit), and FDbar(1 tensor counit)=FD(counit), so the two localized compatibility equations are exactly the transported equations proved in the first step. Full-subcategory data are already instances of the theorem, with their actual Hom modules; the construction uses no faithful-localization or nonempty-object assumptions.

reviewed_lean.note: Every clause of the node matches the Lean, with no stronger assumptions and independent universes. The transported-adjunction formulas are stated on Mathlib's Adjunction.ofNatIsoLeft and agree with its definition. αtilde = FD(γ⁻¹) ≫ α with both transported equations. The four extended functors on the raw ScalarLocalization are pinned by object equalities, pure-tensor formulas and additivity. The localized adjunction's unit and counit are HEq to 1⊗η̃ and 1⊗ε̃, the comparison components are HEq to αtilde and β, and both localized equations hold on all objects with the same a'. The subcategory clause is covered by generality. Edge cases (γ=id, t a unit, B=0, empty categories, n=0) need no extra assumptions. The lean.statement occurs verbatim in the file; there is one sorry and no definitions; docstrings carry the source place, blueprint tag and seven proof steps; no dependency record is touched. No compile was run because no file was changed. Advisory: the 'Second reading by Q112' section is a short self-audit.
